To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the pathological tau isoforms are generated by the cleavage of normal tau by calpain, and the resulting tau fragment is then hyperphosphorylated by GSK3β and CDK5; (ii) the pathological tau fragments are able to form toxic tau oligomers and fibrils; (iii) the pathological tau oligomers are toxic to neurons; and (iv) the pathological tau fibrils are able to seed the formation of pathological tau inclusions in vivo

(1) the toxic gains of function of pathological tau are the primary driver of tau mediated neurogeneration, (2) tau is not required for the initiation and progression of neurodegeneration in AD and related tauopathy models, and (3) tau is a critical regulator of the neuronal cytoskeleton and its loss of function contributes to neurodegeneration in tauopathies.

tau mediated neurodegenration in AD and related tauopathy disorders is driven by the toxic gain of function effects of tau in the disease state and that tau mediated neurodegenerative disease mechanisms are driven by a combination of both direct tau mediated toxic effects on neurons and indirect toxic effects mediated via the induction of neuroinflammation and synaptic dysfunction in the CNS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying neurodegeneration in AD and related disorders.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying neurodegeneration in tauopathies
the mechanisms that underlie the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease ( AD ), a common age related neurodegenerative disease that causes progressive cognitive impairment and dementia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tau mediated neurodegenerative disease mechanisms are complex and multifaceted, involving both toxic gains of function and critical losses of normal functions of pathological tau.
both toxic gains of function of pathological tau and critical loss of normal tau function play a role in the neurodegeneration observed in AD and related tauopathy.
tau mediated neurodegenerative disease is caused by the combined effects of toxic gains of function of pathological tau and losses of normal tau functions in the disease state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are many ways to die from tau, with a multitude of disease mechanisms, and that the disease mechanisms may be differentially engaged in the different tauopathies.

the toxic effects of tau mediated neurogenrative mechanisms are likely the result of complex interactions among multiple gain of function and loss of function effects of the tau protein in the disease state, and that a combination of therapeutic strategies targeting both the toxic gains and losses of function of tau will be required for successful disease modifying drug discovery.

The main takeaway from our work is that
tau is an essential protein for neuronal survival, but that pathological tau is toxic to neurons.

the deleterious consequences of tau mediated neurofibrillary degeneration in AD and related tauopathy disorders are likely to result from a complex combination of both toxic gain of function and loss of function mechanisms.
tau mediated neurodegenerative disease is a complex process that is likely to involve multiple disease mechanisms.
